solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: 'No rule ... forbade' plus 'never mention prices' makes formal/binding easy to eliminate; 'fragile' is the only real distractor and is contradicted by 'for decades'
S030-01.notes: Unspoken but observed agreement = tacit. Formal/binding contradict 'no rule'; fragile contradicts decades of stability. Difficulty mainly vocabulary (tacit).

S030-02.notes: Small size vs. large significance = belied (gave a false impression of). Reflected/determined imply size matches significance; exaggerated is backwards. 'Belied' is a known hard SAT word; students who don't know it may pick reflected.

flags: minor: A is a true supporting detail (classic detail-vs-main-idea distractor); B and C unsupported and unlikely to be picked
minor: factual check OK; fall migrants are typically 3rd-5th generation, so 'may ... be great-grandchildren' is appropriately hedged
S030-03.notes: Text builds to multigenerational round trip; D captures it.

flags: minor: D (too much protein) directly contradicts 'low in protein'; A contradicts 'takes little effort' — easy eliminations leave B vs C
minor: Edmonton 2015 study (Murray et al., PLoS ONE) does report poorer condition and mange with more anthropogenic food — consistent
S030-04.notes: Easy-to-get food is low in needed protein, so content matters more than ease of obtaining. C is an unsupported behavioral prediction.

flags: minor: answer cue — D is the only choice giving percentages for all three treatments, matching 'relative to each building group's starting level'
S030-05.notes: Dot 14/20=70%, UV 18/40=45%, netting 6/10=60%; all percentages in D verified. A (absolute drop) favors UV; B favors netting; C compares final counts only.

flags: minor: factual basis OK (e.g., Udell et al. 2008 on hand-reared wolves and shelter dogs)
S030-06.notes: Text 2 stresses experience with people over inborn domestication effects; C. B extrapolates to chimps (not discussed); D overstates; A reverses.

flags: minor: B copies one note verbatim and states the result but not why it is surprising — the main trap
S030-07.notes: Surprise requires contrast between expectation (12 vs 3 receptors, 4x) and poor result. 12/3=4 correct. C gives only expectation, D the explanation.

S030-08.notes: Benefit (kelp regrowth) vs. drawback (conflict with shellfish harvesters) = concession/contrast; Even so. As a result is the main trap but crab/clam conflict isn't caused by urchin decline.

S030-09.notes: Appositive opened with comma after 'manuscript' must close with comma. Dash mismatches; semicolon splits subject from verb; no punctuation leaves appositive unclosed. Facts OK (radiocarbon 1404-1438; Friedman et al.).

S030-10.notes: Clause after 'noticed that' needs a finite verb; killing has occurred before noticing -> past perfect 'had killed'. 'has killed' clashes with past narrative; C/D nonfinite.

flags: minor: factual check OK — Draupner wave 1 Jan 1995, ~25.6 m with significant wave height ~12 m
S030-11.notes: Sentence 2 is a measured observation contradicting models that called such waves extremely rare. A wrongly labels it exaggerated; B describes sentence 3; C distorts 'more common than once believed' into a change over time.
